claims.claim: The paper reports synthetic trajectories resembling the observed sequences and structured effects of articulatory planning.
claims.limitations: Model geometry, trajectory planning, corpus, and synthetic-to-observed comparison limit claims; matching a trajectory does not identify a unique human motor plan.

claims.claim: The paper reports reduced boundary discontinuities and improved short-frame AEC performance under the tested real-time conditions.
claims.limitations: Echo paths, frame size, batch context, hardware, and evaluation signals bound the claim; continuity on the benchmark is not proof of every room or device.

claims.claim: The paper reports comparative latent conceptual structures across speech, text, and joint models.
claims.limitations: Model choice, layer, analysis method, prompts, and human interpretation bound the claim; a latent cluster is not automatically a human concept.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved multimodal SER generalization over the tested parameter-efficient baselines.
claims.limitations: Datasets, gender labels, task mix, memory policy, modalities, and expression cultures bound the result; auxiliary gender is not a complete model of individual variation.

claims.claim: The paper reports class-incremental classification results against the tested baselines.
claims.limitations: Class order, shots, audio domains, perturbation settings, and memory protocol bound the result; benchmark retention does not establish lifelong robustness.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved continual deepfake detection over rehearsal baselines on new attacks.
claims.limitations: Attack families, auxiliary-label quality, buffer size, stream order, and detector threshold bound the result; no finite memory guarantees future attack coverage.

claims.claim: The paper reports that conventional separators mishandle nonverbal sounds and that the new dataset improves the tested synthetic separation task.
claims.limitations: Synthetic mixtures, labels, scene distribution, separator, and nonverbal taxonomy bound the result; real-film generalization remains open.

claims.claim: The paper reports monolingual models that are competitive with or surpass larger multilingual alternatives on the tested ASR tasks.
claims.limitations: Data volume, speakers, orthography, model size, pretraining compute, and evaluation domain limit generalization to the broader Creole speech community.
